text: 015-D SPIKE COMPLETE (2026-07-29, live/hands-on, post-104-F main 00665738) - daemon 'engram index' cross-file singleton non-persist + CLI response hang. Both symptoms reproduced live: the IPC hang (>270s) is DAEMON/IPC-path-specific (in-process --direct returns ~1s) with H2 confirmed as the mechanism (synchronous long-op response + daemon-spawn/model-load OUTSIDE the client request timeout); the cross-file alpha->beta singleton is ABSENT from the persisted resolved graph (non-persist corroborated; H1 commit-boundary / H4 post-pass-not-invoked OPEN). 104-F does NOT fix it (different layer). Prior direct.rs:162 hypothesis REFUTED. FOLLOW-UP = Ship-owned/instrumented runtime-verification spike: single pre-warmed daemon + validated corpus, trace post-pass invocation/commit boundary + IPC framing to PIN the root cause, then author a fail-safe fix. Do NOT fabricate a fix on an unproven root cause (013-D discipline). Repro procedure + candidate fix directions: docs/decisions/2026-07-29-daemon-index-ipc-hang-spike-findings.md. Deliberation 015-D.

cozo 0.8+ major-version bump to clear the remaining lz4_flex RUSTSEC-2026-0041 advisory (the 1 accepted cargo-audit finding from 102-F). Path: cozo -> swapvec (non-optional cozo dep, pins lz4_flex ^0.10, cannot be feature-dropped like the requests->minreq path). No in-range fix exists at cozo 0.7.6; requires a cozo 0.8+ major bump with graph-backend blast-radius (storage-sqlite/graph-algo API surface). Accepted-with-rationale in docs/decisions/2026-07-28-cargo-audit-advisory-triage.md: swapvec is cozo internal disk-spill (trusted round-trip data, not attacker-controlled). Revisit when cozo publishes 0.8+ or when a patched lz4_flex 0.10.x lands.

Pending-sync drain producer/consumer handoff race (PR #297 Copilot thread lifecycle.rs:466): the bounded snapshot-loop drain_pending_sync_to_completion narrows but cannot close the TOCTOU where a sync caller fails try_start_indexing while a drain owns the lock, is descheduled before publishing pending_sync, and resumes only after the loop's final has_pending_sync peek returns false - the request is then queued with no guaranteed finisher until the next index/sync/watcher tick. Fully closing needs a state-machine handoff (producer atomically registers intent the lock-holder observes on release) rather than snapshot polling. Pre-existing (also affected the prior single-shot drain); mitigated by periodic watcher drains.

Generation-scoped pending-sync queue (PR #297 Copilot thread lifecycle.rs:255): clear_all_pending_sync on hydration cancel / DB-connect-failure is a whole-queue store(0) wipe, not generation-scoped. In the cancel race window (set_workspace installs the new snapshot BEFORE cancelling the old hydration), a sync against the new binding can fail the still-held indexing lock, publish its pending+companion bits, and then have them erased by the old task's clear - silently dropping the caller's explicit --revalidate-code-graph / --backfill-python-canonical until the new generation's own re-scan re-establishes edges. Fix needs generation ownership on the pending queue (ownership tag) or a cancellation hand-off of requests published after the new binding, instead of an unconditional wipe. Narrow race; new-gen full index still yields correct edges.

Stage harvest-provenance doc reconciliation (PR #297 Copilot thread docs/decisions/2026-07-29-stage-harvest-provenance-convention.md:76): the durable convention text asserts a descriptive disposition for stash D2416925 that the archive record (.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl) does not carry - the archived entry stores reason 'archived', not a pointer to the convention. Reconcile the convention wording with the archive record (or backfill the archive reason). Stage-owned planning artifact (arrived in PR #297 base diff via the cycle-3 planning commit e65f352b); out of 104-F implementation scope.

Forced-index reconciliation ordering: evict indexed-minus-discovered file nodes BEFORE the cross-file singleton post-pass (reresolve_calls_edges_with_canonical_context) instead of in the certify block after it. Ref Copilot PR #299 thread PRRT_kwDORJEduc6Usxxl (code_graph.rs:1936). When an excluded-but-still-indexed file duplicates a callee name that has one live def elsewhere, the post-pass runs against the stale pre-eviction set, sees ambiguity, and withholds the cross-file singleton; eviction does not re-run resolution, so a recoverable direct edge stays missing. NOT a regression (pre-103-F the excluded file was never evicted so the post-pass saw the identical ambiguity) and fail-closed (missing edge, never a false edge). Fix: move the U2 eviction loop ahead of the post-pass (gated force||!any_hash_skipped) + add a duplicate-callee-then-excluded recall-RECOVERY test. Touches 082-F/094-F/096-F/101-F post-pass invariants; warrants its own unit + test.

Identify/monitor lz4_flex fix availability to clear RUSTSEC-2026-0041 WITHOUT the cozo 0.8+ major bump (the free 'Option B' path from 017-D). Periodic trigger check: swapvec or cozo re-pins lz4_flex >=0.11.6, OR a patched lz4_flex 0.10.x backport lands in-range for swapvec 0.3's ^0.10 constraint. Chain: engram -> cozo 0.7.6 -> swapvec 0.3.0 (non-optional) -> lz4_flex 0.10.0. When a fix is available, harvest a trivial in-range dependency bump (Cargo.lock update) that clears the last accepted cargo-audit advisory with zero blast radius. Distinct from 99AFF44B/017-D (the heavyweight cozo 0.8+ major bump = Option A). Check via cargo update --dry-run / cargo audit + swapvec/cozo release notes. Refs: docs/decisions/2026-07-28-cargo-audit-advisory-triage.md, docs/decisions/2026-07-29-cozo-0_8-major-bump-feasibility-deliberation.md.

PR#301 review follow-up (099.004-T, src/services/parsing/python.rs:329): qualified staging via python_local promotes calls through is_qualified, attributing callers by first-match find_function_id (code_graph.rs:1767,:2830). Duplicate top-level caller names in one file can stage under an arbitrary duplicate while trusting the canonical target, minting a wrong-origin edge; the bare-call path fails closed via find_unique_function_id. Add ambiguity-aware caller attribution (or preserve the fail-closed check) for qualified staging plus a duplicate-caller regression test. Defensible under 014-D first-match design but a narrow correctness gap.

PR#301 review follow-up (105-F sync/index domain, src/services/code_graph.rs:1335): the index path unconditionally publishes the current topology snapshot even when result.errors holds a transient per-file read failure. A topology-forced descendant that fails to read keeps its old canonical path while the snapshot is published; the next ordinary index sees no topology change and hash-skips the unchanged file, so cleanup is missed. Preserve the absent/old snapshot when a topology-forced file fails, or persist an explicit retry set.

PR#301 review follow-up (105-F sync/index domain, src/services/code_graph.rs:2397,:1537): 099.005-T repaired only the sync path. A non-forced index_workspace parses an empty file, deletes its function metadata, and retracts old 'direct' edges only when force=true; if any other file is hash-skipped the later dangling-edge sweep is also skipped, so the emptied file's raw direct edges survive an ordinary index. Add the same empty-file eviction to the index path plus an index regression with another unchanged file.

PR#301 review follow-up (015-D durable-knowledge accuracy): symptom-1 cross-file singleton non-persist is labeled CORROBORATED in the spike findings frontmatter/summary, but caveat #2 states the known-good --direct path also produced no alpha->beta edge and the minimal corpus was never validated against a known-GREEN singleton. Soften to 'inconclusive pending corpus validation' across docs/decisions/2026-07-29-daemon-index-ipc-hang-spike-findings.md, docs/memory/2026-07-29/stage-cycle4-held-items-memory.md, .backlogit/stash.jsonl, .backlogit/memories.json, and .backlogit/queue/015-D.md; make known-GREEN corpus validation the prerequisite before any persist/non-persist follow-up.
